answer: Bind each identity to one registered racing-pigeon loft in the national register, birds ringed, flights logged, results sealed by a quartz-timed clock. One loft backs one identity; a second claim is rejected, and a loft whose birds never race is struck off. Each fake costs one real loft, 1,100 units for birds, rings, fees, plus 180 days training over the summit ridge; 100 fakes cost 110,000 units and 50 loft-years. Cheapest cheat: renting a keeper to quill-sign a loft to another name; the lender loses the loft backing its own identity, and a borrowed bird's ring fails the register check.
